Motion.blurb: Force-enables VisionMode::Motion so the engine runs frame-to-frame motion detection every vision tick (when the schedule would otherwise leave it off). Without this mode, the MotionDetection_* tunables never run.
Motion.detail: When Motion is on, VisionSystem::DetectMotion calls MotionDetector on the camera image. Results become RobotObservedMotion messages (image centroid, ground-plane centroid, peripheral regions). Used for reactions such as pounce-on-motion and looking toward movement. Pair with the MotionDetection_* group under Vision.MotionDetection to change sensitivity.

MotionDetection_ScaleMultiplier.blurb: Downsamples the camera image before motion detection for speed. 1 = full resolution of the cache size path, higher = smaller (default 4). Range 1–8.
MotionDetection_ScaleMultiplier.detail: ImageCache::GetSize(scaleMultiplier) picks the working resolution. Larger values are cheaper on CPU but blur small motion and make pixel-based thresholds (e.g. MinAreaForMotion_pix) apply on a coarser grid; morphological size is also divided by this scale.

MotionDetection_LastMotionDelay_ms.blurb: Minimum milliseconds between successive motion-detection attempts (default 500). While this cool-down is active, the detector only stores the current frame and does not run frame differencing.
MotionDetection_LastMotionDelay_ms.detail: Prevents flooding from back-to-back detections and reduces false motion caused by residual robot movement after a previous report. Lower = more frequent reports and more CPU; higher = laggier motion events.

MotionDetection_MinBrightness.blurb: Pixels darker than this 0–255 level in either the current or previous frame are ignored for change detection (default 10). Stops dark/noisy regions from counting as motion.
MotionDetection_MinBrightness.detail: Both pixels in a pair must be brighter than this before the ratio test runs. Setting to 0 is asserted invalid at MotionDetector construct. Higher = less sensitive in dim areas; lower = more noise sensitivity.

MotionDetection_RatioThreshold.blurb: Main sensitivity knob: how much brighter/darker a pixel must be vs the previous frame to count as changed (default 1.25). Higher = less sensitive (needs a bigger brightness ratio).
MotionDetection_RatioThreshold.detail: Frame differencing compares current vs previous (after blur). For grayscale, max(a,b)/min(a,b) must exceed this. For RGB, any channel ratio over the threshold marks the pixel. This is the primary control for false positives vs missed motion.

MotionDetection_MinAreaFraction.blurb: Minimum fraction of the (scaled) image that must pass the ratio test before an overall image-motion centroid is computed (default 1/225 ≈ 0.0044). Below this, image centroid is skipped.
MotionDetection_MinAreaFraction.detail: Compared as numAboveThresh > imageElements * MinAreaFraction. Does not by itself emit peripheral motion; peripheral blobs use MinAreaForMotion_pix. Raise to ignore tiny speckles; lower to pick up smaller overall motion.

MotionDetection_CentroidPercentileX.blurb: Horizontal percentile (0–1) used when computing the robust image-motion centroid in image coordinates (default 0.5 = median). Affects reported img_x of RobotObservedMotion.
MotionDetection_CentroidPercentileX.detail: GetCentroid walks motion pixels and picks the percentile along X. 0.5 is center-of-mass style median; other values bias the reported point left/right within the motion blob.

MotionDetection_CentroidPercentileY.blurb: Vertical percentile (0–1) for the robust image-motion centroid in image coordinates (default 0.5). Affects reported img_y.

MotionDetection_GroundCentroidPercentile.blurb: Percentile for ground-plane motion centroid along robot-forward distance after coordinate remap (default 0.05). Comment in code: most important for pounce — prefers motion closer to the robot.
MotionDetection_GroundCentroidPercentile.detail: When both current and previous ground planes are visible, motion inside the ground ROI is masked and GetCentroid is called with swapped axes so that this X maps to distance-from-robot in ground coordinates. Low values bias toward nearer motion for pounce targeting.

MotionDetection_GroundCentroidPercentile.blurb: Percentile for ground-plane motion centroid along the lateral axis in robot coordinates (default 0.50). Used with GroundCentroidPercentileX when projecting motion onto the floor.

MotionDetection_MaxHeadAngleChange_deg.blurb: If the head tilted more than this many degrees between frames (default 0.1°), frame differencing is skipped for that pair — motion would be camera motion, not the world.
MotionDetection_MaxHeadAngleChange_deg.detail: Together with MaxBodyAngleChange_deg and MaxPoseChange_mm, this is a hard gate: head and body must be nearly still, camera not moving, robot not picked up, and LastMotionDelay elapsed, or only the previous-image buffer is updated.

MotionDetection_MaxBodyAngleChange_deg.blurb: Max body yaw/pose angle change (degrees) allowed between frames before skipping differencing (default 0.1°). Stops false motion while turning.

MotionDetection_MaxPoseChange_mm.blurb: Max body translation (mm) allowed between frames for differencing (default 0.5). Tiny moves only — anything larger is treated as robot motion, not scene motion.

MotionDetection_DrawGroundDetectionsInCa.blurb: When true, draws a yellow oval on the camera/Viz view at the image motion centroid sized from ground motion area. Debug overlay only; does not change detection logic.
MotionDetection_DrawGroundDetectionsInCa.detail: Requires a non-null VizManager. Off by default. Useful with MirrorMode / viz camera tools when tuning ground pounce motion.

MotionDetection_MorphologicalSize_pix.blurb: Closing kernel size (pixels at full-res intent, then divided by ScaleMultiplier) used to join fragmented motion blobs before peripheral detection (default 20).
MotionDetection_MorphologicalSize_pix.detail: cv::morphologyEx MORPH_CLOSE on the ratio image. Too small → broken/noisy patches; too large → artificially huge motion regions. Comment in code warns both extremes.

MotionDetection_MinAreaForMotion_pix.blurb: Connected-component area (scaled back toward full-res pixels) must be at least this large to update peripheral motion regions top/left/right/bottom (default 500). Filters speck noise.
MotionDetection_MinAreaForMotion_pix.detail: Uses stat.area * scaleMultiplier compared to this threshold. Separate from MinAreaFraction (overall image centroid). Higher = fewer peripheral activations; lower = twitchier side/top reactions.

MotionDetection_BlurFilterSize_pix.blurb: Box-filter blur kernel size applied to current (and previous if needed) images before ratio testing (default 21). Smooths noise so single-pixel flicker is less likely to count as motion.
MotionDetection_BlurFilterSize_pix.detail: Larger blur = smoother / less sensitive to fine texture; smaller = sharper differencing and more noise. Applied via Image::BoxFilter.

MotionDetectionDebug.blurb: When true, prints extra MotionDetector log lines (found centroid, motion message sent) and can attach debug ratio images. Does not change detection thresholds.
MotionDetectionDebug.detail: Uses PRINT_CH_INFO on channel VisionSystem-style motion logs and may push RatioImg into debugImages. Leave false on a live robot unless diagnosing missed/false motion.

Lasers.blurb: Force-enables VisionMode::Lasers so the laser-dot detector runs when the vision schedule enables it. Still requires the Laser feature gate to be on in product config.
Lasers.detail: VisionSystem only calls DetectLaserPoints if Lasers mode is enabled AND FeatureType::Laser is enabled on the feature gate (COZMO-11185). Detection needs a visible ground plane. Emits RobotObservedLaserPoint. Tune with the Laser_* group under Vision.LaserPointDetector.
Lasers.statusNote: Mode flag is live, but detection is no-op if FeatureType::Laser is disabled or ground plane is not visible.

Laser_scaleMultiplier.blurb: Downsamples the image used for laser-dot detection (default 2, range 1–8). Higher is faster and coarser; min/max radius are area-normalized for resolution.
Laser_scaleMultiplier.detail: Same pattern as motion: ImageCache::GetSize(scaleMultiplier). Coordinates are scaled back when reporting and drawing. Radius area fractions are tuned assuming 320×240, then scaled by image element count.

Laser_minRadius_pix.blurb: Minimum laser blob radius in pixels at the 320×240 tuning resolution (default 2). Converted to a min area fraction so smaller/larger working images stay consistent.
Laser_minRadius_pix.detail: minAreaFraction = π·r² / (320·240). Blobs smaller than that fraction of the current image are discarded after the dual-threshold connected-component pass.

Laser_maxRadius_pix.blurb: Maximum laser blob radius at the 320×240 tuning resolution (default 25). Rejects large bright regions that are not a compact laser dot.

Laser_lowThreshold_normalExposure.blurb: Low brightness threshold (0–255) used in normal exposure to seed connected components for candidate laser spots (default 235). Pixels at/above this form candidate regions.
Laser_lowThreshold_normalExposure.detail: Paired with highThreshold_normalExposure: a component must also contain at least one pixel above the high threshold. Normal vs dark exposure selects this pair vs the _darkExposure pair.

Laser_highThreshold_normalExposure.blurb: High brightness threshold in normal exposure (default 240). A low-threshold blob is kept only if some pixel inside it reaches this level — requires a hot core, not just a large dim region.

Laser_lowThreshold_darkExposure.blurb: Low brightness threshold when the camera is in dark/laser exposure mode (default 128). Same dual-threshold role as the normal-exposure low threshold, but for darker AE settings.

Laser_highThreshold_darkExposure.blurb: High brightness threshold in dark exposure (default 160). Candidate must have a core at/above this value after low-threshold region growing.

Laser_darkThresholdFraction_darkExposure.blurb: For dark exposure, surround pixels must be darker than this fraction of the center pixel brightness (default 0.7) to count as a laser-like dark ring.
Laser_darkThresholdFraction_darkExposure.detail: IsSurroundedByDark samples 8 points around the blob at darkSurroundRadiusFraction × radius. Each must be ≤ center×fraction. Rejects blobs that are not a bright spot on a darker background.

Laser_darkThresholdFraction_normalExposu.blurb: Same dark-ring test as the dark-exposure fraction, used under normal exposure (default 0.9 — surround may be closer to the center brightness).

Laser_darkSurroundRadiusFraction.blurb: How far out (as a multiple of the blob’s equivalent radius) to sample the dark surround ring (default 2.5×). Larger checks a wider halo around the candidate dot.

Laser_MaxSurroundStdDev.blurb: Maximum standard deviation allowed among the eight surround samples (default 25). If the ring is uneven (high variance), the candidate is rejected as not a clean laser spot.
Laser_MaxSurroundStdDev.detail: Compared as variance > MaxSurroundStdDev². Helps reject textured bright patches. Lower = stricter uniform dark ring; higher = more permissive.

Laser_saturationThreshold_red.blurb: When color is available, average red-excess saturation over a scaled bounding box must exceed this (default 30) OR the green threshold — otherwise the bright spot is rejected as uncolored glare.
Laser_saturationThreshold_red.detail: Saturation metric per pixel: max(0, R − max(G,B)). Averaged over ROI. Red or green laser pointers need one channel dominating. Only applied if a color image is present.

Laser_saturationThreshold_green.blurb: Green-channel excess saturation threshold (default 15) for accepting a laser candidate when color is available. Lower than red default — green lasers need less excess to pass.

Laser_saturationBoundingBoxFraction.blurb: Scales the connected-component bounding box (≥1.0) before measuring red/green saturation (default 1.25). Slightly larger box averages color around the core, not only the hot pixels.

Laser_DrawDetectionsInCameraView.blurb: When true, draws laser detection overlays via VizManager (ovals at candidates, surround sample points, circles on accepted points). Debug only; does not change accept/reject math except visibility.

LaserDetectionDebug.blurb: Debug level for laser detection: 0 = off (default), 1 = draw/annotate in camera view tools, 2 = also build separate saliency debug images and extra warnings. Integer, not a bool.
LaserDetectionDebug.detail: At >1, allocates _debugImage from low-threshold components and logs surround/saturation failures. Use briefly when tuning thresholds; level 2 is heavier.
